newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Chinese ship carrying 109 still en route to Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Chinese ship carrying 109 still en route to Bermuda.

text.p: A U.S. Coast Guard cutter continued to tow a crippled Chinese ship carrying 83 suspected illegal migrants and 26 crew toward Bermuda on Monday, two days after the vessel was found adrift in the Atlantic Ocean, the Bermuda government said.
The cargo ship Xing Da, suspected of trying to smuggle migrants into the United States, was expected to reach Hamilton on Tuesday morning, the government said in a statement.
The ship was found drifting on Saturday about 150 miles (240 km) off Bermuda by the U.S. Coast Guard. Officials said the passengers and crew had been aboard since June.

Bermuda government press officer Gavin Shorto said the Xing Da was about 40 miles (65 km) from Bermuda at 9 a.m. (1300 GMT) on Monday and was being towed by the Coast Guard cutter Reliance. It was expected to reach the Bermuda coast on Tuesday morning.

Port officials "are anxious that this vessel should not get mixed up in morning shipping traffic, so we'll probably ask her to slow down a little so as to arrive at Murray's Anchorage at about 10 a.m. tomorrow," he said.

Officials said those on board the vessel were not in need of emergency medical care, but some were dehydrated. Water was flown to the ship. There was no immediate indication on what would be done with the passengers.
